noah: FWIW I hit a streaming-order bug with safetensors-split bundles. Warmup waits for manifest then fails if manifest arrives after first chunk. Reproducer: gs://perf/tests/split-order-2025.log

emily: Oof. That's due to our Loader assuming manifest validation before any chunk handler runs. Two quick fixes: (1) make chunk handler tolerant to missing manifest (buffer minimal metadata), or (2) handshake that guarantees manifest-first from transport.

ravi: I prefer making the chunk handler tolerant. It's a smaller change and works with legacy producers. Plan: buffer only chunk headers (not payload) until manifest arrives, emit lightweight "chunk-announced" events. This allows warmup to begin loading layers that don't depend on manifest-level transforms (like quant-table).

noah: Important: we must avoid unbounded buffering. Add policy: max_announced_bytes default 128KB, eviction LRU by layer priority. If manifest doesn't arrive within manifest_timeout (3s), fail fast with a detailed error.

emily: Also add a transport capability flag so producers that can promise manifest-first can set transport.manifest_first=true. Loader will skip announcement-buffering in that case, saving memory.

ravi: Telemetry: announce.buffer_bytes, announce.evictions, manifest.delay_ms, warmup.early_starts. Canary at 1% then 10% if stable.

ci-bot: Canary build queued: packages/loader/stream-tolerant v0.9 -> canary 1% (job: 7788)

noah: I'll draft the RFC follow-up describing announcement events, buffer eviction policy, and manifest_timeout rationale. Will include a small state diagram. Targeting next-week patch.

emily: Thanks — small clarity: call the events "chunk:announce" and "chunk:payload" in the API doc so downstream consumers can opt-in.

ravi: ack. I'll add unit tests for manifest delayed case and for manifest_first transport bit.
